item.title: EU auditors say uneven enforcement blunts Russia sanctions
item.description: Direct trade with Russia fell from 253 billion euros to 58 billion between 2021 and 2025. The European Court of Auditors calls for clearer rules and stronger monitoring, saying the Commission lacks criteria to judge whether the sanctions work.

item.title: French minister Barrot calls Mélenchon a spokesman for the Kremlin
item.description: The foreign minister said Mélenchon's call for a vote in Donbas disqualifies him from office, and argued the EU budget, not French taxpayers, should carry the cost of backing Ukraine.

item.title: At least 20 dead in two boats off Crete, minister plans EU return hubs
item.description: Frontex says the Libya-to-Crete corridor is now the busiest part of the eastern Mediterranean route, with about 31,800 crossings so far this year, 15 percent fewer than in 2025.

item.title: Ten JEF countries to sign naval partnership pact on 10 November
item.description: The agreement commits the navies, including the Dutch, to joint doctrine, training and planning to deter Russia. It is meant to complement NATO as the United States reduces the forces it would send to Europe in a crisis.

item.title: Hackers use AI in every attack phase, NCTV warns
item.description: The NCTV says a disruptive attack on Dutch society is a matter of when, not whether, in its yearly threat report published on Friday. The cabinet answered with a new action programme the same day.

item.title: Meta, Google and TikTok sue to block California ban on teen feeds
item.description: The three companies filed separate lawsuits on November 4 against Assembly Bill 1709, which takes effect on January 1, 2027. Attorney General Rob Bonta says his office will defend the law.

item.title: German brigade drills in Lithuania with Dutch troops ahead of 2027 stationing
item.description: Exercises Freedom Shield 26-II and Grand Eagle 26 run from 6 November to 3 December, with about 3,800 soldiers from Panzerbrigade 45 taking part. A planning conference this November is to settle the final details for full stationing by the end of 2027.

item.title: Washington's troops are a bonus, not a plan
item.description: One signature and one veto can revoke the American guarantee, as the midterm result and the veto cap showed. The House should write Dutch defence strength into Dutch law now, funded from our own treasury.

item.title: US, Russia, Ukraine in Abu Dhabi talks as Putin refuses ceasefire, Axios says
item.description: The two-day, three-way meeting starts on 10 November, with Kushner and Witkoff leading the US delegation. The Kremlin is not yet ready to have European officials in the room while the UK and France lead forces preparing to secure a peace that does not yet exist.

item.title: We can switch off addictive apps ourselves. The Hague should.
item.description: Brussels has accused Meta of addicting users and fined nobody so far. Kathmann's law passes the judgement to a Dutch parliament, which is exactly where it belongs.

item.title: The House can switch the feed off now, without waiting for Brussels
item.description: Brussels has known for two years and still cannot deliver a binding rule against addictive design. Kathmann's proposal lets our own parliament act, and it does not need permission.
